v.rationale: All three suites pass. Probes checked the timeouts passed to each request, malformed carrier bodies, a 503 followed by a 401, 429/400 responses, whether transient failures get reported, and unusual postcode inputs. impl-1 and impl-3 behave correctly in every probe. Their only gap is that individual rate items are not shape-checked. impl-1 wins narrowly on test hygiene: it blocks real network calls for the whole suite, never sleeps, and asserts exactly what was reported. impl-3 has the most elegant error design (a self-rendering unknown-postcode exception, ShouldntReport, throw match) and the broadest test coverage, but leaves unused imports in tests/Pest.php, does real 100ms sleeps in tests, and doesn't block stray network calls. impl-2 is last: malformed rate items crash it with a 500 instead of serving the fallback, it reports every transient failure (alert noise), it hand-rolls the retry loop instead of using Http::retry, it validates inline, and its 401 test registers a custom reporting hook instead of using Exceptions::fake().
